restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, C = 1626. Fixed register-bank convention: a static bank of at most 2050 words (liveness lemma) holds the circuit values; each gate reads named bank operands and writes its bank result as part of the operation (one primitive; the single-charge reading claimed by winglock bfc8c41, pending review at 124.680), only bank-to-memory transfers are separate loads/stores; START/SB arrays and the trie are main memory, every access charged. The stricter placement-charged reading of #178 (our b001199) prices at 125.3734 for this package's K0 (b001199 itself claims 125.378 at its own K0) and is disclosed in proof Section 8. Not a narrow 64-register file.
Complete SHA3-256 sponge: rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, prefix rounds 0-5, all 256 output bits; 32-byte messages msg(x) = LE32(x); step map f(x) = digest of msg(x).

Van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point search with 256 concurrent chains in the bit slots of a lane-complemented bit-sliced six-round circuit (XOR 23424, AND 3944, OR 4312, NOT 2019, no output fix-ups per 256 evaluations). The fixed encoding complements message/digest lanes 1 and 2; it preserves equality and the DP predicate in lane 3, and digests become the next encoded inputs without transposes or sorting.

DP = digest bits 224..255 zero; trie keyed on bits 0..223; abandonment at 2^40 via sweeps every 2^38 batches; K0 = 65216*2^112; record cap 2^98; drain after the budget; halt at the first RELOCATE; one run.

Charged the exact itemised 34031 operations per 256-evaluation batch (single charge: 33699 gates + 256 digest copies + 72 DP test + 4 control) and 2^13 per chain; T <= 2^124.3803888 < 2^124.381 in every run, certified by the exact integer check A^1000 < 2^124381 * 813^1000 for T = A/813 in lowest terms (proof Section 8). Claimed 124.381. Placement-charged fallback at this K0: 125.3734 (disclosed; b001199's own claim at its K0 = 65400*2^112 was 125.378). Memory < 2^112 bytes. Preprocessing (SETUP + 256 initial SEEDs) 2^8.1485 units, declared 9.

Success >= 0.39050778759 under H-RF only (concurrent-chain lemmas, proof Section 7); reported 0.39 (rounded down, 0.000507 above the 0.39 gate; the right-sizing from our earlier K0 = 65400*2^112 trades success margin 0.00221 -> 0.000508 for 0.004 bits of score, disclosed). Correctness and all resource bounds are unconditional.

Credits: mitchuski for the directly reused 125.58 package; #28 (winglock) DP walk, trie and lemma structure; #148 (may93182) bit slicing; #170 (ercumentyildirim) last-round projection; #178 (zeeshan8281) padding folding and the bank-convention wording; the Keccak team's lane-complement transform supplies the public circuit identity. Unpromoted work, authors credited as coauthors of the reused ideas. No structural cryptanalytic advance claimed.

Three organizer-executed experiments: a 12-bit circuit cross-check, the full algorithm at n=14 (absolute 14-bit collisions), and one n=18 contact run whose count is compared descriptively with the exact random-function prediction 0.28850. No full-width probability is inferred from them.

heuristics.statement: Random-function model for f(x) = SHA3-256-r6(LE32(x)): whenever the algorithm evaluates f at a point not evaluated before, the output is uniform on {0,1}^256 and independent of the coins and of every value revealed earlier in the batch-major, slot-minor order of proof Section 7. Used only to lower-bound the success probability; correctness and resource bounds are unconditional.
heuristics.scope: Six-round prefix SHA3-256 on 32-byte messages (4 variable, 21 constant lanes), iterated from uniform 256-bit starts in 256 concurrent slots, over at most K0 + 256L < 0.9980 * 2^128 evaluations.
heuristics.extrapolation: Standard van Oorschot-Wiener premise, judged plausible for this map in #28. One organizer-executed reduced-width contact experiment on the real map (n = 18) gives a count matching the exact random-function prediction for that harness (proof Section 10). Extrapolated qualitatively to the full 256-bit map; no full-width probability is inferred from the experiment.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is a heuristic: it is false as a literal statement about a fixed function, and six-round SHA3-256 has known differential structure; no evidence that the iterated map departs measurably from a random mapping was found in this survey. The experiments are finite, reduced-width and descriptive, and make no full-width probability inference. The success bound 0.39050778759 holds under H-RF alone.
